_meta.purpose: Verified 2026 operating status per archetype company. The local model has a training cutoff and cannot reach the internet; every fact here was confirmed by web research on 2026-09-09 and carries a source. Generators MUST prefer these facts over model recall.
_meta.sparse_rule: An entity marked sparse has genuinely thin public sourcing. Do NOT invent specifics to fill the gap. EA diagram nodes for sparse entities render dashed with a 'limited public sourcing' note.

companies.name: Waymo LLC
companies.status_2026: Operating commercially and expanding, but freeway operations paused nationwide since 21 May 2026.
facts: 14 US metropolitan areas as of 1 September 2026; Denver, San Diego and Tampa opened to paid driverless public service that day
Miami limited driverless 22 Jan 2026; Orlando 24 Feb 2026, public 15 Apr 2026; Nashville 7 Apr 2026 with a 60-square-mile geofence
~2,500 autonomous vehicles as of Nov 2025; expansion planned to 3,500+ with next-generation Zeekr platform
Nationwide pause of freeway operations 21 May 2026; freeway rides previously available in Phoenix, San Francisco and Los Angeles
IIHS benchmark 23 Jul 2026: 68% fewer police-reportable crashes per vehicle mile than human drivers in the same cities and years
companies.sparse_note: Waymo's production AV stack is trade secret. The ONLY publicly named internal systems are simulation and test infrastructure: Carcraft (simulation replay/scenario engine), Simulation City (higher-fidelity successor), and Castle (reconfigurable closed-course test facility). Do not name any other internal Waymo system.

companies.name: DoorDash, Inc.
companies.status_2026: Operating normally and expanding by acquisition and into autonomy AND aviation.
facts: Completed acquisition of Deliveroo following court approval, effective 2 October
Launched Dot, an in-house autonomous delivery robot from DoorDash Labs, up to 20 mph across bike lanes, roads and sidewalks; early access around Phoenix
Partners with Serve Robotics for sidewalk autonomous delivery, and with Wing for drone delivery (tens of thousands of deliveries completed)
Launched DoorDash Air after earning its own FAA Part 135 air carrier certificate, becoming the eighth US drone operator to do so
companies.cross_archetype_note: DoorDash holds a Part 135 certificate itself. The boundary between 'delivery marketplace' and 'drone operator' is not clean in 2026; LM and DD domains legitimately overlap for this company.

companies.name: Bird (brand of Third Lane Mobility, Inc.)
companies.status_2026: NOT an independent going concern. Restructured post-bankruptcy; operates as a brand under a new parent.
facts: Filed Chapter 11 in December 2023, two years after a SPAC listing that valued it at ~$2.3B
Avoided liquidation; reorganised in 2024 under new parent Third Lane Mobility Inc., which also holds the Spin brand
Liquidating plan confirmed 2 Aug 2024, effective 17 Sep 2024; as of Feb 2026 the Tort Claims Trustee reported 101 of 221 asserted tort claims resolved
Post-restructuring model is deliberately regulator-friendly with capped fleet sizes to avoid prior over-expansion
Bird and Spin together operate in ~350 cities across Canada, the US, Europe and the Middle East
companies.modelling_note: Bird is the POST-RESTRUCTURING, permit-constrained micromobility archetype. Do not model it as a growth-stage scale-up. Its distinguishing processes are fleet-cap compliance, permit retention and unit-economics discipline.

companies.name: Lime (Neutron Holdings, Inc.)
companies.status_2026: Newly public, operationally profitable, but carrying a disclosed going-concern warning.
facts: Filed for IPO 7 May 2026; completed Nasdaq Global Select Market IPO in July 2026 under ticker LIME
FY2025 revenue $886.7M, +29% YoY; operating income swung from a $24.6M loss in 2023 to $70.4M profit in 2025
Q1 2026 revenue $170.2M (+32% from $129.0M); Q2 2026 revenue $304M (+24% YoY)
2025 average operational fleet 325,137 vehicles; Revenue per Vehicle per Day (RVD) $7.47; ~230 cities across 29 countries
2025 operational fleet retention rate 116% (won more fleet capacity in existing cities than it lost elsewhere)
S-1 disclosed substantial doubt about ability to continue as a going concern absent IPO proceeds to service debt

companies.name: Bolt Technology OÜ
companies.status_2026: Operating normally; largest European scooter operator by city count. Also a ride-hail platform.
facts: Over 230,000 scooters and e-bikes across more than 270 European cities
Launched its first fully in-house e-bike in January 2026
Rolling out AI-equipped e-scooters for compliant-riding enforcement, first phase in Germany, Belgium and Switzerland (April 2026)
Milan licence for scooters, e-bikes and cargo bikes running to 2026: ~2,000 scooters, 2,000 e-bikes, 15 cargo bikes
Liverpool City Council contract from early 2026 — first UK scooter launch — 2,000 scooters and 100 e-bikes
Reports at least 15% durability improvement in regular operations from simplified internal components
companies.modelling_note: Bolt is the healthy, vertically-integrated micromobility archetype (designs its own hardware) and simultaneously a ride-hail marketplace. It is the best archetype for MF processes that assume a going concern.

companies.name: Joby Aviation, Inc.
companies.status_2026: PRE-REVENUE, pre-certification. Furthest along of the US eVTOL field.
facts: Cleared Stage 4 of the FAA type certification process in late March 2026 — scrutiny shifts from design documentation to physical hardware
Began flight testing its first FAA-conforming aircraft for Type Inspection Authorization (TIA) in March 2026
FAA pilots expected at the Marina, CA facility to conduct TIA testing
Type certificate anticipated late 2026 by management; independent analysts place realistic entry into service mid-to-late 2027
Commercial launch additionally requires FAA air carrier certification of Joby's operating entity, vertiport operational readiness in at least one market, and sufficient aircraft production
companies.sparse_note: No commercial service has ever operated, so there is no operational literature. Certification-stage facts are well sourced; day-to-day operating processes are necessarily forward-looking. Mark forward-looking steps as such.

companies.name: Archer Aviation Inc.
companies.status_2026: PRE-REVENUE, pre-certification. Phase 3 of 4 in FAA type certification.
facts: Completed Phase 3 of 4 of the FAA Type Certification process for the Midnight eVTOL; first eVTOL manufacturer to reach this stage
FAA issued the newest Midnight aircraft a special airworthiness certificate; piloted VTOL campaign underway, progressing toward piloted transition flight
Preparing for potential early Midnight operations with partners in Florida, Texas and New York as soon as H2 2026
Participating in the White House eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) for US city deployments
UAE GCAA transitioned Midnight into a Restricted Type Certificate (RTC) programme for entry into service in the UAE
Holds an FAA Part 135 air carrier certificate permitting it to operate a commercial airline

companies.name: Wisk Aero LLC (Boeing subsidiary)
companies.status_2026: MOST PRE-COMMERCIAL of the archetypes. Pre-revenue, autonomous, certification targeted 'before the end of the decade'.
facts: Generation 6 completed its maiden flight 16 December 2025 at 12:26 PST from the Hollister, CA flight test facility
Second Gen 6 aircraft flew 4 May 2026, putting two Boeing-backed certification aircraft into simultaneous flight test
Gen 6 is the first-ever candidate for FAA type certification of an autonomous, passenger-carrying eVTOL in the United States
Four passengers; operated with human oversight from the ground rather than an onboard pilot
Launch markets identified as Houston, Los Angeles and Miami
Plans to certify before the end of the decade — materially later than Joby or Archer
companies.sparse_note: Wisk is the sparsest entity in this wiki. It has never carried a paying passenger, its autonomy stack is not public, and its ground-supervision concept of operations is not published in operational detail. Almost all Wisk-specific processes are forward-looking. Render Wisk EA nodes dashed.

facts: Passed 2 million cumulative deliveries in January 2026 (1 million reached in 2024); world's largest autonomous delivery operator
US deliveries growing ~15% week-over-week for the seven months preceding January 2026
Raised $600M in January 2026 and a further $200M in March 2026
Platform 2 in customer service since January 2025: hovers at ~300 feet and lowers orders on a tethered droid; up to 8 lb payload, ~10-mile radius
P2 launched in Pea Ridge, Arkansas and the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex; Seattle announced
Walmart partnership across 17 DFW locations, offering drone delivery to up to 75% of the DFW population
Restaurant partners include Panera, Chipotle, Crumbl, Blaze Pizza, Wendy's and Little Caesars
